rules.comment: Workaround for a Colemak bug in the Claude app: https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/68859. Note: the macOS Colemak input source re-translates Karabiner's output, so to send the app Cmd+K we emit key_code n (Colemak maps the n-position to 'k'). Digits are not remapped by Colemak, so Cmd+3 is emitted as-is.
rules.description: Claude app: Cmd+J -> Cmd+K, Cmd+3

rules.comment: Clicks the project selector on the New Conversation screen. Claude's Electron renderer exposes no accessibility tree, so the button cannot be targeted by name and the position is hardcoded. Coordinates are absolute on the main display, so this only lands correctly while the Claude window sits in its usual position and size. The cursor is left on the button rather than returned: restoring it needs a spawned script to read the cursor before Karabiner moves it, and the hold covering that read measured p50 101ms against a 300ms tail and one 963ms over 400 samples -- a race, not a margin, and 200 of the rule's former 300ms. mouse-click.js is not an option here: a Karabiner-spawned script's CGEventPost does not move the pointer on this machine (probed: posted a move 80pt away, cursor did not move), though CGWarpMouseCursorPosition and reads both work. The warp-to-click gap was 100ms and is now 0 -- 0ms opened the selector 10 times out of 10, and an always-visible target hit-tests correctly even though a warp posts no hover event. The click clears its modifiers because the physical Command is still down when it is posted, and the trailing vk_none keeps the button from being the last `to` event, which would hold it down and drag.
rules.description: Claude app: Cmd+P -> click project selector (physical key r in Colemak)

rules.comment: Clicks the Create PR button in the session view. Like the Cmd+P project-selector rule, the Electron renderer exposes no accessibility tree, so the position is hardcoded. Coordinates are absolute on the main display; y matches the project-selector rule, x is the button's position in a 2x Retina screenshot (1313 px) halved to points. The cursor is left on the button rather than restored: restoring it needs a spawned script to read the cursor before Karabiner moves it, and the 200ms hold covering that read measured p50 101ms against a 300ms tail and one 963ms over 400 samples -- a race, not a margin. Dropping the restore removes the spawn, the hold and the race together. The 100ms warp-to-click gap stays: without it the click races the cursor move and the app registers only the hover, so the shortcut had to be pressed twice. Unlike the Cmd+P gap, which measured 0, this one has not been driven to its floor -- the target is the Create PR button, so a binary search would fire it once per press.
rules.description: Claude app: Cmd+Shift+P -> click Create PR button (physical key r in Colemak)

rules.comment: Show Diff. The app ignores Cmd+Shift+D while the chat box has focus, so the rule first clicks an empty spot in the sidebar to blur it. Like the Cmd+P and Cmd+Shift+P rules, the coordinates are absolute on the main display and only land correctly while the Claude window sits in its usual position and size. The cursor is left in the sidebar rather than restored: restoring it needs a spawned script to read the cursor before Karabiner moves it, and the 200ms hold covering that read measured p50 101ms against a 300ms tail and one 963ms over 400 samples -- a race, not a margin. Dropping the restore removes the spawn, the hold and the race together. Neither hold is needed: 0ms for both the warp-to-click gap and the click-to-keystroke gap opened the diff 10 times out of 10. The sidebar spot is always on screen, so the click races nothing, and the Cmd+Shift+D that follows is queued behind the click rather than competing with it -- the same reason the menu-bar sequences need no pauses. The expectation that the second gap was waiting on focus actually moving was wrong.
rules.description: Claude app: Cmd+Shift+G -> click empty sidebar (230, 940), Cmd+Shift+D

rules.comment: Archives the current session via the command palette. This replaces the earlier Cmd+Shift+E -> Cmd+Shift+E rule that reached the app's effort picker; the effort picker now stays on its default position (physical e, the key that types 'f' in Colemak). Cmd+K is emitted as key_code n for the same Colemak re-translation bug as the Cmd+J rule (https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/68859). The letters after it are ordinary text typed into the palette's search field, and text input always goes through the macOS Colemak input source, so each letter is emitted as the physical key that types it: 'arch' = a s c h, with a, c and h unchanged by Colemak. Enter is not remapped by Colemak. The query is 'arch' rather than 'archive' because every letter costs: each one is a render the app owes before it will look at Enter, and the shorter query measured about 50ms less input backlog while still putting the Archive row first. The 150ms after Cmd+K gives the palette time to open and focus its search field; it is unmeasured, but it held at 100% CPU load, and it is the one to raise if letters ever land in the composer instead of the palette. The 120ms before Enter is the whole point of the rule, and is the measured floor. The palette inserts its contextual Archive '<title>' row asynchronously, once the query resolves; until that lands the primary action is New chat '<query>' (its Enter badge turns red), so an early Enter creates a chat and sends the query as its first message instead of archiving anything. How it was measured, without spending a real archive per trial: swap the Enter for a harmless marker key at the same offset, record at 60fps, and read whether the Archive row was present in the frame the marker landed in. Each press then yields not just pass/fail but the delay it actually needed -- nominal minus the gap between the row appearing and the marker landing -- so a batch run at a generous 300ms measures the whole distribution uncensored, which a sweep cannot: a press at 50ms can never reveal that it needed 90. At 100% CPU load that requirement was 17-83ms over 19 presses (one further press at 100ms nominal landed in the same frame as the marker, so 83-117ms), and the 60fps capture resolves to 17ms, which puts the floor at 100ms and makes 120ms the smallest value consistent with every observation. That the number is unchanged from the old rule is a coincidence worth stating plainly: the old rule failed at 120ms because it typed seven letters, and this one holds at 120ms because it types four. What 19 hand presses cannot see is the far tail -- a one-in-500 press on a worse day than any tested -- so if this ever misfires again, raise this hold rather than suspecting the rest of the sequence. One caveat on the floor itself: it was measured with a marker keystroke standing in for Enter at the same offset, and that proxy has only been checked against a real Enter in the failing direction (it predicted 3/3 failures that the real Enter then reproduced), never in the passing direction. Enter runs the palette's command handler while the marker goes into the text field. A batch of real presses at 120ms under load would close that gap. Cmd+1 afterwards navigates to the first chat, with 150ms after Enter for the archive to complete and the palette to close first, so the shortcut lands on the chat list rather than the closing palette. Digits are not remapped by Colemak, so 1 is emitted as-is. The trailing vk_none keeps Cmd+1 from being the last event, since Karabiner holds the last event down until the from key is released and a held key would repeat into whatever has focus.
rules.description: Claude app: Cmd+Shift+E -> Cmd+K, type 'arch', Enter, Cmd+1 (physical key k in Colemak)

rules.comment: Drives the app's own View menu from the menu bar, because neither direct route works: the Claude app holds Cmd+Tab and Ctrl+Tab for Next/Prev Chat and will not give them up to a native macOS App Shortcut override, and emitting the menu items' Cmd+Option+Arrow accelerators collides with Spectacle's global window arrangement shortcuts, which win before the app sees them. fn+Ctrl+F2 moves focus to the menu bar, 'v' type-selects the View menu, Down opens it, 'prev'/'next' type-selects the item, and Enter activates it. The Down is load-bearing and was found empirically: type-select only highlights the menu title, it does not open the menu, so without it the following letters keep type-selecting along the menu bar row and Enter fires on whichever title is highlighted by then (observed: the Window menu opened). Digits are not remapped by Colemak, so the from side is used as-is. The letters are type-select input and so go through the macOS Colemak input source, exactly like the Cmd+Shift+E archive rule's palette text, so each is emitted as the physical key that types it: 'v' is unchanged by Colemak, 'prev' = r s k v, 'next' = j k x f. There are deliberately no pauses between the events. The rule shipped first with 150/150/150/120ms, which worked but felt slow; a probe of the same sequence at 0ms then passed 20 of 20 presses, so those constants were covering nothing. Menu tracking runs a modal event loop that consumes the event queue in order, so each event waits for the stage before it rather than racing it, which is why the floor is zero rather than merely small. No margin was added on top: a margin over a measured floor of zero would be covering a race that was shown not to exist, at the cost of latency on every press. The 20 presses were unloaded, so if this ever misfires, suspect a busy renderer delaying the menu and measure before adding a constant back. The trailing vk_none keeps Enter from being the last event, since Karabiner holds the last event down until the from key is released and a held Enter would repeat into whatever has focus.
rules.description: Claude app: Cmd+Shift+1 -> menu bar, View > Previous Sidebar Tab; Cmd+Shift+2 -> menu bar, View > Next Sidebar Tab

rules.comment: Clicks the Always apply link in the toast that Shortwave shows in the bottom-right corner after a label is applied, which promotes that one-off into a standing rule. The toast offers no keyboard shortcut, so the mouse is the only route. The link is visible for as long as the toast is up rather than only on hover, so a plain warp and click lands on it and the slower mouse-click.js walk is not needed. The cursor is left on the button rather than returned: restoring it needs a spawned script to read the cursor before Karabiner moves it, and the hold covering that read measured p50 101ms against a 300ms tail and one 963ms over 400 samples -- a race, not a margin, and 200 of the rule's former 300ms. mouse-click.js is not an option here: a Karabiner-spawned script's CGEventPost does not move the pointer on this machine (probed: posted a move 80pt away, cursor did not move), though CGWarpMouseCursorPosition and reads both work. The warp-to-click gap was 100ms and is now 0 -- 0ms opened the selector 10 times out of 10, and an always-visible target hit-tests correctly even though a warp posts no hover event. The click clears its modifiers because the physical Command is still down when it is posted, and the trailing vk_none keeps the button from being the last `to` event, which would hold it down and drag. The click clears its modifiers because the physical Option is still down when it is posted, and the trailing vk_none keeps the button press from being the last to event, which would hold the mouse button down until Option+A is released and drag instead of click. Coordinates are absolute on the main display and only land correctly while the Shortwave window sits in its usual position and size and the toast is showing.
rules.description: Shortwave: Option+A -> click Always apply on the label toast (1272, 890)

rules.comment: Archives the top notification in the Inbox side panel by handing the whole gesture to a script, which moves the pointer there with real mouse events and clicks. Karabiner's own set_mouse_cursor_position warps the cursor without posting a mouse-moved event, and that is the root of every problem this rule has had: Chromium does not update its hover target from a warp, so the archive button, which only exists while the row is hovered, is either not armed or no longer armed when the click lands, and the click hit-tests against the row underneath and opens the notification instead. Waiting it out does not work reliably, because the window is bounded at both ends. Measured from the warp, with a single click: 60-80ms is too early and hits the row, 130ms archives, 250ms archives with false negatives, 400-500ms fails outright, and 150ms managed 1 in 4, so the window is narrow, drifts, and is not worth aiming at. An earlier two-click version appeared to work by firing at two offsets and landing one inside the window, which also means it archives twice whenever both land. The script sidesteps the window by walking the pointer in steps with CGEvents, which Chromium treats as genuine motion. Posting CGEvents needs Accessibility permission, which osascript does not have on its own, but Karabiner does and the processes it spawns inherit it; run the same command from a terminal and the events are silently filtered and the pointer never moves. It also clears the modifier flags on the click, since the physical Cmd+Shift are still down and an uncleared click arrives as Shift+Click and extends the text selection across the page, and it restores the cursor itself. Notion has no keyboard shortcut for archiving a single notification, so the mouse is the only route. Coordinates are absolute on the main display and only land correctly while the Notion window is top-left aligned at its usual size with the Inbox panel open; y is measured from the top of the first row rather than its middle, so it holds regardless of how tall the notification is, and the three buttons sit about 10 points apart, so shift x by 10 if the click lands on a neighbor.
rules.description: Notion: Cmd+Shift+E -> click archive on top notification (166, 135) (physical key k in Colemak)

rules.comment: Opens the emoji picker for the last received message, so any emoji can be sent as a tapback without touching the mouse. The hover tapback bar is anchored to the message bubble, so it moves with the message's width and height and no fixed coordinate can reach its picker. The right-click menu is anchored to the click point instead, so the rule right-clicks a fixed point on the last message and works from there. (360, 890) sits inside the last received bubble whatever its size: received bubbles are left aligned at x 348 so a short message still covers x 360, and the transcript is bottom anchored so the bubble's lower edge stays at y 900 however tall the message is. A sent message is right aligned and will not be hit. move-to-tapback-picker.js then reads the menu's own window frame rather than assuming where it landed, because macOS pins the menu above the bottom of the screen and the height it pins from changes with the menu's items, so a message carrying a link would otherwise be off by the height of the extra ones; if no menu appears it leaves the pointer alone and the click lands back on the message. The right-click is held for 150ms rather than clicked instantly, which is what makes it reliable: the menu opens on the mouse down and starts a modal tracking loop, and an immediate mouse up can arrive before that loop is installed and dismiss it, which failed 5 times in 6 before the hold and 0 times in 6 after. Karabiner posts both clicks itself because it holds Accessibility and the osascript it spawns does not, which is also why the script only warps the pointer. The 200ms hold lets restore-mouse-position.js read the pointer before it moves, the 100ms hold keeps the right-click from racing the cursor move, and the 550ms hold covers osascript startup, measured at 70-110ms, plus the script's 250ms poll for the menu. Coordinates are absolute on the main display and only land correctly while the Messages window sits in its usual position and size with the conversation scrolled to the bottom; a group conversation indents received bubbles past x 360.
rules.description: Messages: Cmd+E -> open the emoji picker for the last received message (physical key k in Colemak)
